Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 84, verse 6–12:

The meaning of His saying, ﴿O man, you are laboring toward your Lord with labor, and you will meet Him﴾: that is, striving toward Him through your deeds. Al-kadh (exertion) is a person's work and effort in a matter, whether good or evil, until that matter leaves its mark on him, that is, it affects him. Qatadah, al-Kalbi and al-Dahhak said: "You are working for your Lord with a work, ﴿and you will meet it﴾," that is, you will meet the reward of your deed, whether good or evil.

﴿As for him who is given his record in his right hand﴾: his register of deeds [[In "b": his deed.]] ﴿he will be called to a light account﴾. Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) related to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam related to us, Nafi' informed us, from Ibn Umar: Ibn Abi Mulaykah related to me that Aishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, would not hear anything she did not know without returning to it until she knew it. She said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever is brought to account will be punished." Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, does not Allah, Mighty and Majestic, say: ﴿he will be called to a light account﴾?" She said: He said: "That is only the presentation (of deeds). But whoever is scrutinized in the reckoning will be destroyed" [[In "b": whoever is scrutinized in the reckoning, the reckoning destroys him.]] [[Reported by al-Bukhari in Knowledge, chapter "Whoever hears something and returns to it until he knows it," 1/196-197, and in the commentary of Surah al-Inshiqaq, and in al-Riqaq. Muslim in Paradise and its Bliss, chapter on affirming the reckoning, no. (2876), 4/2204. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/131.]].

﴿And he will return to his family﴾: that is, in Paradise, among the wide-eyed maidens (hur 'in) and the human women ﴿joyful﴾ [[188/a]] because of what he has been given of good and honor.

﴿As for him who is given his record behind his back﴾: his right hand will be chained to his neck and his left hand will be placed behind his back, so his record will be given to him in his left hand from behind his back. Mujahid said: His left hand will be dislocated from behind his back.

﴿He will call out for destruction﴾: he will cry out for woe and ruin when he reads his record, saying: "Woe is me! Ruin is mine!" Like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They will call there for destruction﴾ [al-Furqan: 13].

﴿And he will burn in a blaze﴾: Abu Ja'far, the people of Basra, Asim and Hamzah recited "wa yaslā" with a fatha on the ya and light (tashdid-less) sad, like His saying: ﴿who will enter the greatest fire﴾ [al-A'la: 12]. The others recited it with a damma on the ya [and a fatha on the sad] [[Omitted from "a".]] and a shaddah on the lam, like His saying: ﴿and the burning of a hellfire﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 94] and ﴿then throw him into the hellfire﴾ [al-Haqqah: 31].

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 84, verses 20–21:**

His statement, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿So what is wrong with them that they do not believe?﴾ is an interrogative of denunciation (*istifham inkar*, a question expressing rebuke).

﴿And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate?﴾ Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: "They do not pray."

Abu 'Uthman Sa'id ibn Isma'il al-Dabbi informed us: Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Jabbar ibn Muhammad al-Jirahi informed us: Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mahbubi related to us: Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi related to us: Qutaybah related to us: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah related to us, from Ayyub ibn Musa, from 'Ata' ibn Mina, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "We prostrated with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in *Iqra' bi-ismi Rabbika* and in *Idha al-sama' infatarat*."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Prayer, chapter on prostration: 3/165; Muslim in Mosques, chapter on prostration of recitation (*sujud al-tilawa*), no. 578, 1/406; Abu Dawud in Prayer, chapter on prostration in *Idha al-sama' infatarat*, 2/118; al-Nasa'i in Prostration of the Qur'an, chapter on prostration in *Iqra' bi-ismi Rabbika*, 2/161; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 3/301.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliji informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us: Musaddad related to us: Ma'mar informed us, saying: "I heard my father say: Bakr related to me, from Abu Rafi', who said: 'I prayed the 'Atamah prayer with Abu Hurayrah, and he recited *Idha al-sama' infatarat*, and he prostrated. I said: What is this? He said: I prostrated in it behind Abu al-Qasim (ﷺ), and I will not cease prostrating in it until I meet him.'"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Prostration of Recitation, chapter on whoever recites a prostration verse in prayer and prostrates with it, 2/559; and Muslim in Mosques and Places of Prayer, chapter on prostration of recitation, no. 578, 1/407.]]
